set.st: The Minnesota DNR's water-trail notes for the Granite Falls to Hwy 4 stretch say a gold vein found near Patterson's Rapids in 1894 set off a short rush; the vein soon played out and the boom town of Springville became a ghost town. GNIS keeps the name Gold Mine Lake here, and the USGS mineral database's Delhi gold prospect (gold in hornfels) is about 600 m away, likely the same vein. Charles Patterson's trading post of about 1783 stood at the rapids. A mining boom, not a buried cache; the Redwood Gazette covered it from 1894 to 1898. In Aug 1894 Fred Schroeder deeded 14 acres to Minneapolis buyers for $3,000 for the "Springville Quartz" mine, and others bought land across the river from it. The Gazette describes the 14-acre tract as granite taking in half of Spring Lake, on the Minnesota River 9 miles north-west of Redwood Falls; by 1896 it was the Minnesota Gold Mining and Refining Co. with shafts and an engine; on 16 November 1898 the paper called Springville a deserted mining town with a shaft house and thousands of tons of quartz piled beside a crusher, apparently never milled. No assay result was ever printed.
set.t: Hunt the camp ground, not the vein: coins, tokens, tools and bottles where the miners lived. The edge of range, about 3 hours from Eau Claire. Private land: check who owns the river bank first. Look for the shaft house footing, the crusher base and the quartz pile; they are the camp's hard features.
pinev: Pin is the GNIS Gold Mine Lake point; the camp itself is not placed
The USGS Delhi gold prospect is about 600 m away
The Spring Lake of 1894 is evidently today's Gold Mine Lake, 9 miles NW of Redwood Falls; the shaft house and crusher stood on the 14-acre tract on its shore.
set.tovw: Lead grade C: a documented 1894-98 mining camp with three period papers and a named 14-acre tract on Gold Mine Lake; the camp ground itself is not pinned.

src: Redwood Gazette, 30 Apr 1896, p. 4 (Minnesota Gold Mining and Refining Co.)
